@graph.alternativeHeadline: Answer-engine optimization is a layer on top of SEO, not a replacement: priority order and budget guidance for AI startups
@graph.description: AEO is not a replacement for SEO. For AI startups in 2026, the right sequence is: fix technical SEO first, add AEO content structure, then build GEO credibility signals through earned press coverage. This playbook covers what each term means, what Google actually says, where they overlap, and where to spend first.
keywords: how to get cited by ChatGPT

itemListElement.name: AEO vs SEO: What Startups Actually Need in 2026

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between AEO and SEO for startups?

acceptedAnswer.text: SEO (search engine optimization) is the foundation: making your site technically crawlable, building domain authority, and earning keyword rankings in Google. AEO (answer-engine optimization) is a content and structure layer on top of SEO that helps AI-driven surfaces like Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity extract and cite your content directly. If your SEO is broken, AEO will not compensate. The right order is: fix SEO basics first, then add AEO structuring, then build GEO credibility signals through earned press and entity recognition.

mainEntity.name: Does Google say startups need to do something different for AI Overviews?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google's own June 2026 guidance states plainly that there is no separate trick for AI Overview placement. The same fundamentals that earn traditional organic rankings earn AI Overview inclusion: helpful, reliable, people-first content with demonstrated expertise and genuine authority signals. AI Overviews pull from the same index as regular search. A page that can't rank on page one of a Google SERP is not going to get cited in an AI Overview.

mainEntity.name: What is GEO and how is it different from AEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: GEO (generative engine optimization) is the practice of optimizing for citation and named mention inside the generated answers that AI engines produce, rather than just the links they return. AEO is about structuring content so engines can extract your answer. GEO is about building the credibility signals (earned press coverage, named authorship, cited statistics, third-party corroboration) that make engines confident enough to name you. The Princeton GEO study found a 30 to 40 percent citation uplift from content with attributed statistics and clear expert sourcing.

mainEntity.name: How does earned press coverage affect AI search citations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Earned press coverage is the primary source of entity signal that AI engines use to decide who to cite on a given topic. If CoinDesk, Forbes and Blockworks have all written about your company in a consistent framing, the engine treats that framing as reliable. If only your own site makes the claim, the confidence is much lower. In the launches I have run, companies with 10 or more tier-1 placements consistently surface in ChatGPT and Perplexity answers within 60 to 90 days. Companies with no press footprint do not, regardless of how well their AEO is structured.

mainEntity.name: Where should an AI startup spend first: SEO, AEO, or PR?

acceptedAnswer.text: In order: technical SEO baseline, then content creation with AEO structuring and named authorship, then earned press coverage as entity fuel, then GEO monitoring and iteration. With a $5,000 to $10,000 monthly budget, allocate roughly 60 percent to earned press, 30 percent to content, and 10 percent to technical cleanup. The content without entity signal will not get cited by AI engines. The press coverage without good content to link back to will not convert. Both are required, and the leverage is higher in earned media than in content optimization alone at the early stage.
